title: Anterior tooth-loss location adds no demonstrated diabetes-prediction benefit beyond total tooth loss across two NHANES cycles
abstract: We asked whether anterior concentration of missing natural permanent teeth improves diabetes-status prediction beyond total tooth loss and conventional nonlaboratory predictors. Source-only logistic models in NHANES2011–2012 (n=2774) were frozen and tested in separately recruited2013–2014 (n=2995). Diabetes status combined self-reported diagnosis and HbA1c≥6.5%. Adding anterior missing-tooth count changed target MEC-weighted Brier score from 0.104362 to 0.104388, delta +0.000025; joint source/target rescaled-PSU bootstrap95% interval [-0.000348,+0.001131]. This incremental-prediction test is negative, not an equivalence result or a refutation of published site-specific associations. It does not compare with glycemic screening or establish causality.
